article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Morning Brief
article.dek: Broncos win the Thursday night game in overtime, Lamar Jackson looks likely out again Sunday, and the Week 6 board is live with all three headline cards.

items.headline: Broncos win the Thursday night game in overtime
paragraphs: Denver beat Seattle 17-14 in overtime on Thursday night. Ja'Quan McMillian picked off Sam Darnold at the Seattle 43 in the extra period, and Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yarder to win it.
The Broncos move to 4-2. The Seahawks fall to 3-3 — two straight losses for the defending champs.
items.takeaway: The opener is settled: Broncos 17, Seahawks 14 in OT. Denver +2.5 covered and the total stayed under 40.5. The app has already pulled the lines, so this game is off your board.

items.headline: Quarterback roundup: Hurts out, Lamar likely out again, Williams expected back
paragraphs: Jalen Hurts is out Sunday against Carolina with a blood clot in his calf. Tanner McKee starts for the Eagles, and the app's quarterback snapshot already shows McKee.

Lamar Jackson missed practice again Thursday — that's four straight sessions missed. Tyler Huntley is the likely starter Sunday at Cleveland. One honest flag: the app still lists Jackson as the expected starter, so it has not caught up to Thursday's news yet.
Baker Mayfield is out again, so rookie Jalon Daniels starts for Tampa Bay against Pittsburgh. The app has Daniels listed.
Better news in Chicago: Caleb Williams practiced fully Wednesday and Thursday and is expected back Sunday at Atlanta. Michael Penix was full too and says he's good to go.
items.takeaway: Inactive lists post about 90 minutes before each Sunday kickoff. Ravens-Browns (Lamar) and Bears-Falcons (Williams) are the two to watch — Sunday's brief will carry the final designations.

items.headline: Sunday weather: clear and mild everywhere
paragraphs: No games today, so this is a look ahead to Sunday. The National Weather Service has sunshine and mild temperatures for every outdoor venue: Cleveland 62F, Philadelphia 57F, Foxboro 54F after some morning frost, Tampa 77F, Kansas City 66F, Green Bay 63F.
items.takeaway: Nothing in the forecast changes how you read Sunday's games. File it as clear and move on.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The Week 6 board is live — here are the three cards
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Bills moneyline -218 (DraftKings) over the Raiders. The model gives Buffalo a 71.8% chance to win, reliability MEDIUM. That's the card that forgoes value to chase win probability — and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced: Giants moneyline -104 (FanDuel) over the Saints. Model 65.3% vs the market's 50.0%, MEDIUM. This is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, and a good starting point if you're new. Note this changed overnight: the evening board had Packers moneyline here.
Value: Falcons +1.5, -110 (FanDuel), against the Bears. This is the model's plus-EV play at +2.4% EV, MEDIUM reliability.
items.takeaway: Three cards, three different jobs. Hit Rate = which supported pick looks most likely to win. Balanced = a strong pick without paying too much. Value = the model's plus-EV play. Pick the job that fits yours.

items.headline: Your book's price doesn't match the card? Tap Check
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, but your book is its own animal. If the line or price you can actually get doesn't match the card, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator.
What you get is a bet-or-no-bet verdict on YOUR price — a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Two house rules while you're in there: odds are price mechanics only. -218 means every $2.18 you risk wins $1. And the app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive your staking is — it's deliberately conservative, so let it do that job.
items.takeaway: Check turns any price you can actually get into a fresh verdict. Use it before you bet, not after.

items.headline: Learn the Game: tickets vs handle
paragraphs: Two words you'll see next to every betting split. Tickets — sometimes labeled BET — is the share of individual bets placed on a side. Handle — labeled HND — is the share of dollars wagered on a side.

Here's a clearly labeled hypothetical. Imagine 100 bets totaling $10,000 on a game. Seventy bets ($2,000 total) are on Team A, and thirty bets ($8,000 total) are on Team B. Team A has 70% of the tickets but only 20% of the handle. Team B has 30% of the tickets but 80% of the handle.
Same game, two different stories. The crowd is on Team A; the bigger dollars are on Team B.
items.takeaway: When most tickets land on one side but most of the money lands on the other, the market is split — and that disagreement is exactly what a Fade section hunts for. (The example above is hypothetical, not real betting activity.)

items.headline: Overnight move: Chiefs -8.5 down to -7.5
paragraphs: The one real move since the evening edition: Kansas City drifted from -8.5 to -7.5 on DraftKings against the Chargers — a full point toward the underdog. The morning board already has the new number, so the app caught it.
The books don't fully agree, though. FanDuel still shows Chiefs -8.5 and Pinnacle sits at -8.0. If you like Kansas City, -7.5 is a better buy than -8.5 — shop it.
items.takeaway: A point of line move with the books split. If you want the Chiefs, take the -7.5, and tap Check on your book's actual number before you do.

items.headline: Everything else parked — with one number to watch
paragraphs: Quiet everywhere else since the evening board: Panthers -3.5, Steelers -2.5, Rams -12.5, Colts -7 (DraftKings), 49ers -7.5, Patriots -7.5, Packers -1.5, Texans +2.5, Falcons +1.5. No moves worth chasing.

The one to watch: Ravens -3.5 at Cleveland hasn't budged even with Lamar Jackson likely out again. If Baltimore rules him out, watch whether that number finally moves — the market is pricing in a decision that hasn't been announced yet.
items.takeaway: Quiet boards are fine. The edge is knowing which number to keep an eye on: Ravens -3.5, pending the quarterback call.

items.headline: Thursday night is settled and off the board
paragraphs: Final: Broncos 17, Seahawks 14 in overtime. Denver +2.5 covered, and 31 total points kept it under 40.5.
The app has pulled the game from the board — it now shows in-progress/final with no lines. Nothing to price, nothing to chase.
items.takeaway: The opener is closed out. Sunday's board is where the work is now.

items.headline: Sunday's final answers arrive Sunday morning
paragraphs: Friday is practice reports and probabilities. The actual answers — who's in, who's out — come from the final injury designations and then the inactive lists, which post about 90 minutes before each Sunday kickoff.

The board refreshes every morning and evening, and Sunday's brief will carry the final calls. Don't lock in a Sunday bet tonight and skip the morning read — especially on Ravens-Browns and Bears-Falcons, where the quarterback decisions are still open.
items.takeaway: No Sunday bet is final until the inactives and the morning board are in. Read Sunday's edition first.

items.headline: Honesty nudge: the tracker only works if you do
paragraphs: Settlement is manual — nothing auto-settles in NFL EDGE. The tracker only works if you're honest with it. Log the losers too. Your record is only as honest as your entries.
items.takeaway: Every bet in the tracker, win or lose. Especially the losers.

evidence.fact: Denver Broncos beat the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime on Thursday Night Football at Empower Field at Mile High. Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal with 4:53 left in OT after Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold at the Seattle 43. Denver moves to 4-2; Seattle falls to 3-3.
evidence.interpretation: Denver +2.5 covered; the total of 40.5 went under (31 points scored).
evidence.app_guidance: The game is final and its lines are off the board — nothing left to price.

evidence.fact: Jalen Hurts is out for Sunday's home game vs Carolina (superficial blood clot in calf). Tanner McKee starts at quarterback for Philadelphia, and the app's quarterback snapshot confirms McKee as the expected starter.
evidence.interpretation: The Eagles' offense runs through a backup on Sunday.
evidence.app_guidance: The app's lines and QB snapshot already reflect McKee starting.
